attempts.label: CRCNS:hc-29
attempts.entry_title: Reward biased spatial representations in lateral septum and CA1 (Wirtshafter and Wilson 2020)
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data, because the dataset holds sorted spike times but no position tracking, which every spatial analysis needs. Untested for that reason are the lower spatial information and scarcer place fields of lateral septum than CA1, the skew of fields by direction of travel toward reward, the excess of lateral septum fields on the rewarded choice side, and the stronger CA1 to lateral septum cross-correlations there. The unit counts hold in part: the files hold exactly the paper's 452 lateral septum and 178 CA1 clusters, though some septal clusters are exact copies of others. The counts of cells meeting the paper's inclusion criteria also need position.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Wirtshafter and Wilson (2020) on CRCNS hc-29, which holds the sorted spike times of 452 lateral septum and 178 CA1 clusters and the time bases of 57 recordings of six rats. The data set holds no position data, so every finding of the paper beyond the count of units recorded, which matches, is blocked; the notebook counts the units and checks the files, finding spike trains deposited many times and clusters that hold the spikes of others.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Wirtshafter and Wilson (2020) from CRCNS hc-29

outcomes.statement: 452 caudodorsal LS units and 178 CA1 units were recorded in six rats, of which 165 CA1 and 378 LS cells met the spike rate and track coverage criteria.
outcomes.source: Results, opening paragraph; Results, Place fields are less abundant, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: we recorded the activity of 452 caudodorsal LS units and 178 CA1 hippocampus units in six male Long Evans rats
outcomes.notes: Two of the four counts are tested and both match exactly. The data set holds 452 LS and 178 CA1 clusters, the paper's two counts of units recorded, from six rats (LS from rats 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 12; CA1 from rats 10 and 12 only). Of the 452 LS clusters 42 are byte for byte copies of other clusters (two rat 7 trains deposited 18 and 25 times, one rat 6 pair), leaving 410 distinct trains, within the tolerance of 45 when only byte for byte copies are discounted; dropping as well the 14 largest clusters of rat 6's tetrode 26, which hold the spikes of the others, and the multi-unit cluster MUA9 leaves 395, outside it. The outcome rests on the clusters deposited, which the paper's 452 matches exactly and so evidently counts. All 178 CA1 trains are distinct. The other two counts, 165 CA1 and 378 LS cells meeting the rate and track coverage criteria, are untested (data_missing). They need the rate above 12 cm/s and the coverage of the track under either reading the criterion names, and so the animal's position and speed, which the data set does not hold. The criterion needs all four counts, so the claim holds in part. Over whole recordings 423 LS and 166 CA1 clusters reach 0.05 Hz, a variant that decides nothing, as the paper's rule counts only time above 12 cm/s. The first version of this record gave the claim as blocked; it was changed after verification round 1 (see verifications).
deviations: Units are counted as the cluster fields deposited, copies included; the count of distinct spike trains is shown beside it.
The two counts of cells meeting the rate and coverage criteria are not computed, for lack of position and speed.

findings.statement: The data set holds no position, speed or direction data, and no trial, lap or epoch markers. The paper's Methods describe position tracked at about 30 Hz by overhead cameras, and every finding from Figure 2 on (rate maps, spatial information, place fields, direction of travel, maze location, laps, and the matching of CA1 and LS fields for the cross-correlations) uses it, so none of the paper's findings beyond the counts of units recorded can be tested on the data set. The data description names only spikes and time files, and the paper's Data availability names only this data set.

In rat 7, two spike trains, of 1033 and 1441 spikes, are deposited byte for byte under 18 and 25 cluster names, across 16 of the 19 rat 7 recordings with clusters and three tetrodes (18, 27 and 32). The copies cannot all be the recordings they are filed under, as 27 of them hold spikes after the end of their recording's timestamps (5403 spikes in all, none before the start), and these are the only spikes in the data set outside their recording. The 452 LS clusters, the paper's count, include these 41 copies.

Several clusters hold the spikes of others. On rat 6's tetrode 26, in each of the 14 recordings with clusters there, the largest cluster holds at least 99.6% of the spikes of each other cluster on the tetrode (47 of 47 such clusters), as if a cluster of all spikes were deposited beside the units; two of these clusters (2017-05-01, cl_7 and cl_9) are identical. Over the data set 89 pairs of clusters on one recording share at least 99% of the smaller train's spikes within 0.5 ms. A further 24 pairs on neighbouring tetrodes (LS 29 and 30, 21 and 22; CA1 1 and 6, in rats 7, 9, 10 and 12) share 71.5 to 98.5% of their spikes, against a median of 0.5% (at most 1.3%) for the same pairs with one train shifted by 1 s, so the same unit or the same noise was probably sorted twice. The data set does not say which clusters are single units, and of its 630 clusters 588 are distinct trains.

Times.mat is described only as "time files for all sessions". It holds 57 continuous time bases of the six rats, most at 0.512 ms intervals, six of rat 6 at 3.2 ms and one of rat 7 at 0.0512 ms, lasting from 2.5 min to 31 h, while the paper analyses one 30 min maze session a day. Nothing marks which part of a recording is the maze session. Read whole, no recording changes its sampling interval or has a gap of 0.1 s, so the time bases do not mark the session. Between its first and last spike no recording has a stretch of 60 s without a spike from any of its clusters (45 of the 46 recordings with clusters checked; rat 7's 2017-08-02 holds only copies of the trains deposited many times). The spikes begin within 0.09 h of each recording's start; in rats 7, 8 and 9 they span 0.5 to 0.9 h, which may be the session, though nothing says so, while in rat 6 they span up to 4.9 h and in rats 10 and 12 the whole 3.8 to 6.4 h recording. Eleven recordings have no cluster. The sampling intervals are not stated. The six rat 6 recordings at 3.2 ms have 25 brief gaps of 4.9 to 93 ms, and two of them repeat timestamps (1121 in 3 s of 2017-04-21, 3280 at the end of 2017-04-26).

The cluster names follow the pattern the description gives (session date, tetrode, cluster) with the rat and a session suffix, but ten names of rat 7 (2017-07-21, tetrode 28) write cl1 for cl_1, and one LS cluster of rat 9 is labelled MUA9, a multi-unit label, with no description of what it holds. The CA1 clusters come from two of the six rats (10 and 12), which neither the description nor the paper states. Tetrodes 1 to 16 are CA1 and 17 to 32 LS, which the files show but the description does not say.

disagreements.reason: Cell 16 counts 452 LS and 178 HPC clusters from 6 rats, which equals the paper's numbers exactly; 410 LS trains are distinct, still within ±45. The other two counts (165 CA1 and 378 LS cells meeting the rate and coverage criteria) need speed and track coverage, and neither reading in the criterion can be computed without position. The whole claim is labelled blocked, although half of it was tested and matches exactly; a label of partially_reproduced, with the inclusion counts blocked, would describe the result more accurately (problem 1). The 452 is a count of deposited LS entries, not units, with 42 extra copies of identical trains and a MUA9 multi-unit cluster, and 410 distinct trains is still within tolerance (problem 2). rate_hz is computed over the whole recording, labelled a variant that decides nothing, which is correct (problem 3).

entries.name: wirtshafter-2020
entries.title: Reward biased spatial representations in lateral septum and CA1 (Wirtshafter and Wilson 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Wirtshafter and Wilson (2020) on CRCNS hc-29, which holds the sorted spike times of 452 lateral septum and 178 CA1 clusters and the time bases of 57 recordings of six rats. The data set holds no position data, so every finding of the paper beyond the count of units recorded, which matches, is blocked; the notebook counts the units and checks the files, finding spike trains deposited many times and clusters that hold the spikes of others.
